findings.title: setUTCMonth overflows on month-end anchor dates, producing wrong renewal dates
findings.explanation: setUTCMonth does handle month/year rollover, but it does not clamp the day of month. For Jan 31, setUTCMonth(1) yields Feb 31, which normalizes to Mar 3 (or Mar 2 in leap years). Likewise Mar 31 -> Apr 31 -> May 1, Aug 31 -> Sep 31 -> Oct 1, and so on. The removed code explicitly clamped to the last day of the next month (Jan 31 -> Feb 28/29). This is a billing regression: customers anchored on the 29th, 30th or 31st would get billed days late and the period would drift or be inconsistent. The PR description's claim that setUTCMonth 'already handles' this is incorrect for day overflow. Restore the clamping, e.g. compute the last day of the next month with Date.UTC(year, month + 2, 0) and use Math.min(anchorDay, lastDay), or set the date to 1 before setting the month and then set the day to the clamped value.

findings.title: No tests covering month-end and year-rollover cases
findings.explanation: This change alters billing behavior for edge cases but adds no tests. Add unit tests for Jan 31 (non-leap and leap year), Mar 31, Apr 30, Dec 31 -> Jan 31 (year rollover), and a mid-month date such as Jan 15. These would have caught the overflow regression immediately.

findings.title: Clamping rationale comment was removed along with the logic
findings.explanation: The deleted comment documented an intentional business rule (renewals clamp to the last day of the next month). If the simplification is retained in any form, keep a comment stating this rule so future refactors do not silently remove it. Also consider whether the anchor day should be preserved across periods (e.g. Jan 31 -> Feb 28 -> Mar 31) rather than derived from the previous period start, since chained calls will otherwise drift to the 28th permanently; that likely needs the original anchor day to be passed in or stored.

findings.title: Redundant Date copies
findings.explanation: Both start and end are constructed from periodStart separately, which is fine, but if the code is reworked, a short helper like addMonthsClamped(date, n) would make the intent clearer and be easier to unit test in isolation.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Simplify next billing period calculation

Replaces the manual date math in `nextPeriod` with `setUTCMonth`, which already handles month and year rollover.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/services/billing.ts b/src/services/billing.ts
index 81ad02d..eb1824d 100644
--- a/src/services/billing.ts
+++ b/src/services/billing.ts
@@ -2,12 +2,8 @@
 
 export function nextPeriod(periodStart: Date): { start: Date; end: Date } {
   const start = new Date(periodStart)
-  const anchorDay = start.getUTCDate()
-  const year = start.getUTCFullYear()
-  const month = start.getUTCMonth() + 1
-  // Clamp to the last day of the next month, so a period starting on Jan 31 renews on Feb 28/29.
-  const lastDayOfNextMonth = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month + 1, 0)).getUTCDate()
-  const end = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month, Math.min(anchorDay, lastDayOfNextMonth)))
+  const end = new Date(periodStart)
+  end.setUTCMonth(end.getUTCMonth() + 1)
   return { start, end }
 }
```
